questionText:
Consider the productions $A \rightarrow PQ$ and $A \rightarrow XY$. Each of the five non-terminals $A, P, Q, X,$ and $Y$ has two attributes: $s$ is a synthesized attribute, and $i$ is an inherited attribute. Consider the following rules.

Rule 1: $P.i = A.i + 2$, $Q.i = P.i + A.i$, and $A.s = P.s + Q.s$

Rule 2: $X.i = A.i + Y.s$ and $Y.i = X.s + A.i$

Which one of the following is TRUE?
options: Both Rule 1 and Rule 2 are L-attributed.
Neither Rule 1 nor Rule 2 is L-attributed.
explanation:
Definition of L-attributed Definition:
A Syntax-Directed Definition (SDD) is L-attributed if each attribute evaluation rule for a production $A \rightarrow X_1 X_2 \dots X_n$ computes:
1. A synthesized attribute of $A$.
2. An inherited attribute of $X_j$ using ONLY:
- Inherited attributes of the parent $A$.
- Any attributes (synthesized or inherited) of symbols $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_{j-1}$ to the left of $X_j$.

Evaluating Rule 1 ($A \rightarrow PQ$):
- $P.i = A.i + 2$: Inherited attribute of $P$ depends on parent's inherited attribute $A.i$. (Valid)
- $Q.i = P.i + A.i$: Inherited attribute of $Q$ depends on left sibling $P$ and parent's inherited attribute $A.i$. (Valid)
- $A.s = P.s + Q.s$: Synthesized attribute of head $A$ depends on attributes of children. (Valid)
Hence, Rule 1 is L-attributed.

Evaluating Rule 2 ($A \rightarrow XY$):
- $X.i = A.i + Y.s$: Inherited attribute $X.i$ depends on $Y.s$, which is to the right of $X$ (right sibling). In L-attributed SDDs, dependence on right siblings is strictly prohibited.
Hence, Rule 2 is NOT L-attributed.

Thus, Only Rule 1 is L-attributed.
